_comment: Wavelength grids used to SIMULATE observations (--mock). With --data the
wavelengths come from your file and only 'resolution' is read from here;
'sampling' says what the step means: 'wavelength' (default) makes it a
spacing in Angstrom; 'velocity' makes it a step in km/s, giving a grid
Only points inside a line-emulator window contribute residuals, so
segments outside those windows do not enter the likelihood.
'resolution' is a single resolving power for one entry. Real instruments
whose arms differ in R (X-Shooter) need one entry per arm; naming more
than one entry on the command line (--instrument name1 name2 ...)
combines them into a single fit, with each line broadened at whichever
named instrument's wavelength range covers it. Combined instruments'
segments must not overlap, and no line window may straddle the boundary
between two of them -- move the boundary if one does.

dense.description: Dense uniform-wavelength mock grid spanning every emulator's full predictable range (min(lambda_min) to max(lambda_max) across all 37 line emulators -- CIV1169b sets the blue edge at 800 A, HEI7065 the red edge at 7190 A); a numerical grid, not an observational setup.
dense._note: A constant 0.033 A step is a varying velocity step: about 12.4 km/s at 800 A, 2.5 km/s at 4000 A, 1.4 km/s at 7190 A. Still oversampled for R = 10000 throughout (pixel step stays below the ~30 km/s resolution element even at the blue edge, just with less margin than in the middle of the range). About 1.9e5 points.

Martins2017_stars_uv.description: Realistic wavelengths and resolution to create the spectra from stars from Martins 2017; UV segment.
Martins2017_stars_uv._note: One arm of the Martins2017_stars setup; use together with Martins2017_stars_opt (--instrument Martins2017_stars_uv Martins2017_stars_opt) to fit or simulate the full UV+optical spectrum in one run, split at 3400 A.

Martins2017_stars_opt.description: Realistic wavelengths and resolution to create the spectra from stars from Martins 2017; optical segment.
Martins2017_stars_opt._note: One arm of the Martins2017_stars setup; use together with Martins2017_stars_uv (--instrument Martins2017_stars_uv Martins2017_stars_opt) to fit or simulate the full UV+optical spectrum in one run, split at 3400 A.

LMC_stars_R17500.description: Far-UV segment of the LMC O-star spectra (Sk -66 171, Sk -69 50), R = 17500; holds the PV 1118 line.
LMC_stars_R17500._note: Resolving powers of the five LMC segments are those listed per line in each star's own line_list.txt. The 3.5 km/s step is the median velocity sampling of the observed spectra. With --data the wavelengths come from the file and only the resolving power and wavelength range are used. Use all five LMC_stars_* entries together.

LMC_stars_R45800.description: Far-UV segment of the LMC O-star spectra, R = 45800; holds the lines from CIV 1169 to CIV 1550.

LMC_stars_R30000.description: Mid-UV segment of the LMC O-star spectra, R = 30000; holds NIV 1718 and NIII 1750.

LMC_stars_R6700.description: Blue optical segment of the LMC O-star spectra, R = 6700; holds NIV 3480 through HeII 5411.

LMC_stars_R11400.description: Red optical segment of the LMC O-star spectra, R = 11400; holds OIII 5592 through HeI 7065.
